newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina House gives final OK to baseball vote.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina House gives final OK to baseball vote.

text.p: The North Carolina House gave final approval for a referendum allowing Forsyth and Guilford counties to vote on a baseball stadium tax.
The measure passed 74-39 in a second reading Thursday after lawmakers added an amendment that would protect either county from bearing the entire burden if only one approved the tax.

The amendment requires the tax to be approved in both counties in order to take effect. If approved in a May 5 referendum, the proposal would levy a one percent tax on restaurant meals in the two counties and add a 50-cent surcharge to stadium tickets.
It would create a stadium financing district to issue revenue bonds for the $210 million facility. Public funding would be capped at $140 million. Private investors have pledged the rest.
The stadium district would be created and the tax levied only if the investment group wins a major league baseball expansion team in 1999 or buys an existing team.
The proposal now goes to the Senate, where it is expected to win approval.
